stem: A canopy review uses only one center-room photograph to claim uniform recovery after work. What evidence would most improve the conclusion?
choices: Repeat the center-room photograph after the same recovery interval so the before/after comparison uses the same viewpoint.
Document the training technique and date because consistency of technique is the main determinant of recovery quality.
Collect repeatable observations across predefined mapped canopy positions and relate them to the authorized work, baseline, and recovery timing.
Use fixture wattage and room-average environmental data as the primary evidence that canopy recovery was uniform.
rationale: One center-room image cannot establish uniformity across a canopy. A stronger evaluation uses predefined locations, repeatable viewpoints or measurements, and a known relationship to the authorized work and recovery interval. That makes spatial differences visible and allows before/after comparison. Repeating one central photo improves consistency but still cannot represent the whole canopy.
